name: Chalk stained by iron round a fossil (the mould of an ammonite or an urchin)

diffuseAlbedo.source: Munsell 10YR 7/4 (very pale brown), chalk stained by iron oxide round pyritised fossils as field descriptions give it
diffuseAlbedo.note: No measured colour of the site's own ground was read: a first colour from the Munsell notation field descriptions give the layer, converted approximately.

refractiveIndex.note: The host is chalk calcite, and the iron-oxide stain is a minor phase. As for chalk, reconcile this with the 1.6003 in travertine.json and cream-marble.json.

porosity.source: Wikipedia 'Chalk' citing Hancock 1975 (porosity 35-47 %); Bloomfield et al. 1995, QJEGH 28, S131 abstract (https://nora.nerc.ac.uk/7752/, mean 34.0 %)
porosity.note: This is the host chalk's matrix porosity. The proposal's claim that the stain 'does not change it measurably' is unsupported: iron oxide can partly fill pores. Nothing was read on this, so treat 0.41 as an upper bound for the stained zone.

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.source: Wikipedia 'Chalk' citing Hancock 1975: fragments 10-100 microns, plates 0.5-4 microns
grain.note: The same body as the chalk.
grain.derivation: The largest common fragments are 0.1 mm

bed.source: Docs/Stages/cube.md section 7, row 'Chalk': 'bedding partings every 0.37' (read, line 344)
bed.note: A design value, as for the chalk.
bed.derivation: The stage rule's parting spacing, 0.37 m

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, Journal of Geophysical Research 117, B08409 (fault surfaces, 0.6 to 0.8; cited in Stone.ush)
hurst.note: The middle of the range measured on rock surfaces, as the topsoil's.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
